task.title: M10: Animated runtime trace view (play a recorded or live trace over the graph and map)
task.description:
The visualization half of the Capacitor runtime trace POC. Given a trace file (or a live stream from codeviz serve) in the M10 trace format, animate the Graph and Map views: at each tick, files and modules that executed light up with intensity by call count, runtime edges draw as animated pulses from caller to callee, and everything idle fades back over a configurable decay. Play/pause, speed, and a scrubber over the recorded range; live mode follows the stream with a 'follow' toggle. Two static summaries over the whole trace: an overlay color mode 'executed' (total calls per file, reusing the M8 overlay plumbing) and an edge classification over the import graph: import edges that carried calls, import edges that never did, and runtime edges with no import edge (dependency injection, callbacks, event handlers, which run opposite to the import direction). The third class is drawn in its own style because it is the thing the static graph cannot show.

Acceptance criteria:
- 'codeviz serve --trace trace.jsonl.gz' adds a Trace control strip to the Graph and Map views; hash params view=graph&trace=1&t=<ms> make a moment linkable.
- Playback of a 60-second Capacitor browser trace at 1x stays above 30 fps on the Map view with 150 files; ticks are batched so the view never re-lays out, only restyles.
- Live mode: with the harness streaming, the view updates within one tick of capture.
- Summary mode shows the three edge classes with a legend and counts, and the 'executed' overlay appears in the color-mode selector.
- Works on the static export when the trace is exported alongside snapshots (recorded only).
- One test for the tick batching/decay reducer. No new runtime dependencies.
